question: In the lecture, the function \(f(x)=1\) if \(x\) is irrational and \(f(x)=0\) if \(x\) is rational is claimed to be discontinuous at every real number. Explain, using the definition of continuity, why this is true for an arbitrary point \(c\in\mathbb{R}\).

Consequently, the limit cannot be a single value, and it certainly cannot equal \(f(c)\) (which is either \(0\) or \(1\)). Therefore \(f\) is discontinuous at every real number.
